svg.title: Grassroots Direct Action: The Sit-In Wave (1960), SNCC & The Freedom Rides Route (May–Nov 1961)
svg.desc: Zoomed Eastern and Southern United States GIS atlas map with Canada, Cuba, The Bahamas, Mexico, and Great Lakes, charting the February 1960 Greensboro sit-in wave, the April 1960 founding of SNCC in Raleigh, and the May 1961 CORE and SNCC Freedom Rides highway route from Washington D.C. through Anniston, Birmingham, and Montgomery to Jackson, Mississippi.

text.tspan: Ella Baker Guides Founding of SNCC
13 CORE Riders Depart to Test Boynton Ruling
Bus Firebombed • Bull Connor & KKK Mob
First Baptist Church Mob • 600 US Marshals
Mass Arrests Force Federal Transit Desegregation

g.text: Greensboro (1 Feb 1960), Raleigh SNCC & Nashville Riders
D.C. → Carolinas → Atlanta → Anniston → Birmingham → Jackson
Anniston firebombing, Birmingham mob & 600 US Marshals
Deep South Resistance Core vs Upper South
Culminating in Nov 1961 ICC interstate desegregation order

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · PAPER 3 (OPTION 33) · KT2.1: SIT-INS & THE FREEDOM RIDES
Grassroots Direct Action: Sit-Ins (1960), SNCC & The Freedom Rides (May–Nov 1961)
Following the 1960 Greensboro Sit-Ins (70,000+ protesters) and founding of SNCC, CORE & SNCC Freedom Riders braved Anniston firebombs,
Birmingham/Montgomery mobs, and 300+ Parchman prison arrests to force JFK, RFK, and the ICC (Nov 1961) to enforce Boynton v. Virginia.
